name: architect
conclusion: architect (Ask) specifies 5 of 5 categories: 7 autonomy limits, 8 clarification rules, 4 approval gates, 10+ validation rules, 10+ escalation rules. Strongest: validation rules.

autonomy_limits.conclusion: 7 autonomy limits (7 mandatory, 0 advisory; 1 conditional), mostly prose: re-allocating the feature directory; Agent-dispatching Socratic questioning; Agent-dispatching the Layer Impact phase.

statements.quote: You do NOT re-allocate a feature directory — `/spec` already did that, and `/architect` inherits the F<NNN> + feature_path from the existing `state.yaml`.
You MUST NOT attempt to Agent-dispatch Socratic questioning, gray-area resolution, section drafting, or the Definition of Ready validation; those operations live in this skill.
**This phase is INTERACTIVE and MUST NOT Agent-dispatch.**
**No automatic Read** of any path a contract string might name — a contract string is recorded verbatim, never fetched (directory-traversal defense, mirroring the user-flow gate).
Do not write an ADR with a slug containing path separators or shell metacharacters.
Do not overwrite the file wholesale.
NEVER re-allocate the feature directory — `/architect` inherits from `/spec`'s prior allocation. Exit non-zero if `state.yaml` is missing.

clarification_rules.conclusion: 8 clarification rules (8 mandatory, 0 advisory; 1 conditional), mostly prose: writing the design before clarifying questions; six architect questions one at a time; vague answers before proceeding.

statements.quote: You NEVER start writing the design before asking clarifying questions.
**Phase 1 Step 3: Ask six architect-style questions, ONE AT A TIME via Pattern B (the visual marker)** — do not batch them into a numbered list.
Do NOT proceed until the user has answered all six. If any answer is vague, ask a follow-up using the same Pattern B marker:
Then resolve them ONE AT A TIME using `AskUserQuestion` (Pattern A — multi-choice is a perfect fit for gray areas because each has 2-4 enumerable options from the research).
Wait for ALL gray areas to be resolved before proceeding.
Either way, YOU never fabricate the answer — you force the human to make it (BR-014).
Ask the user (Pattern A) whether this feature's Layer Impact Analysis should be a HARD /build gate on unfilled CRITICAL items, or advisory (warn-only) — mirroring F006's `design_mandatory`:
NEVER start writing the design before asking clarifying questions.

approval_gates.conclusion: 4 approval gates (4 mandatory, 0 advisory; 0 conditional), mostly list: gating on a missing architecture baseline; section approval via AskUserQuestion; each section before moving on.

statements.quote: Then reuse the **existing contract-completeness WARN+recorded-override machinery** (BR-006; do NOT fork a parallel mechanism) to gate proceeding.
**Prompt for approval via `AskUserQuestion`** using the standard section-approval template below.
ALWAYS present each section for user approval before moving to the next.
Wait for the user's selection before executing anything.

validation.conclusion: 10+ validation rules (10 mandatory, 0 advisory; 2 conditional), mostly list: architect-specific Definition of Ready checklist; clear module boundaries; named integration patterns.

escalation.conclusion: 10+ escalation rules (10 mandatory, 0 advisory; 9 conditional), mostly prose: missing interactive-user-input standard; missing architecture standards files; missing spec-allocated feature directory.
